summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with acute pancreatitis triggered by secretin administration during an MRCP, presenting with epigastric pain radiating to the back and nausea. She was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and IV pain control, then gradually advanced to a soft diet as symptoms resolved. Her pancreatic cysts remained stable on imaging, and biliary irregularities improved. Fludrocortisone was adjusted to 0.1 mg BID to prevent hypokalemia, and midodrine was held during admission per patient preference. She was discharged home in good condition, tolerating oral intake, with instructions to avoid fatty foods and monitor for fever or vomiting.
